# askfirst results (generated by `python -m askfirst.report`)

Test: 48 weeks, 1,460,477 ordering decisions (22.1% had zero demand). Train 3,272,702, calibration 1,038,622 decisions.

## Forecast accuracy (WAPE on test weeks, lower is better)

| forecast | WAPE |
|---|---|
| model | 0.363 |
| mean4_naive | 0.385 |
| lag52_seasonal_naive | 0.662 |
| lag1_naive | 0.418 |

## Calibration

80% interval coverage on test: 79.6% overall; 78.6% on the 10% of decisions with the highest value of review; 79.7% on the rest.

| department | 80% coverage | order-up-to target | achieved |
|---|---|---|---|
| FOODS_1 | 79.9% | 42.9% | 50.3% |
| FOODS_2 | 78.9% | 42.9% | 49.1% |
| FOODS_3 | 80.0% | 42.9% | 49.4% |
| HOBBIES_1 | 78.9% | 78.9% | 77.3% |
| HOBBIES_2 | 80.0% | 78.9% | 80.0% |
| HOUSEHOLD_1 | 79.4% | 78.9% | 77.3% |
| HOUSEHOLD_2 | 79.8% | 78.9% | 78.3% |

## Autonomy frontier (planner removes 50% of the model error; router assumes the same)

Reviewing every decision would cut the shortage and surplus cost by 50.0% (before paying for the reviews).

| ranking rule | share of that saving captured at a 5% / 10% / 20% review budget | review share needed for 50% / 80% of it |
|---|---|---|
| random | 5.1% / 10.0% / 20.2% | 50% / 81% |
| widest interval first | 2.8% / 6.0% / 11.4% | 70% / 93% |
| highest value at stake first | 27.0% / 38.1% / 53.1% | 18% / 49% |
| expected cost of acting alone | 28.5% / 39.9% / 55.4% | 17% / 47% |
| expected value of review (askfirst) | 28.6% / 40.0% / 55.5% | 17% / 47% |
| expected value of review, planner profile known | 28.5% / 39.9% / 55.4% | 17% / 47% |
| oracle (upper bound) | 38.9% / 52.6% / 69.3% | 9% / 31% |

95% confidence intervals from resampling the test weeks (10% budget): expected value of review (askfirst) 40.0% [39.5%, 40.5%]; expected cost of acting alone 39.9% [39.5%, 40.4%]; highest value at stake first 38.1% [37.6%, 38.6%]; widest interval first 6.0% [5.7%, 6.3%]; random 10.0% [9.9%, 10.2%]. Expected value of review minus highest value at stake: 1.9 points [1.6, 2.1].

Spearman correlation of the value-of-review score with the expected cost of acting alone: 0.9996 (uniform planner), 0.887 (planner who helps most where a price drop or event is visible).

### When the planner is better or worse than the router assumes

| planner | all-human saving | askfirst capture at 10% | oracle capture at 10% |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.3 | 30.0% | 40.0% | 52.6% |
| 0.5 | 50.0% | 40.0% | 52.6% |
| 0.7 | 70.0% | 40.0% | 52.6% |
| context | 48.5% | 40.1% | 52.8% |
